Hacksaw , Audiocast , Q3'25

2025-11-04 09:30

Hacksaw

Operator
00:00 - 00:17

Welcome to Hacksaw's Q3 earnings call for 2025.

During the questions and answers session, participants are able to ask questions by dialing Pound Key five on their telephone keypad. Now, I will hand the conference over to Group CEO, Christoffer Källberg, and CFO, Per Alnefelt. Please go ahead.

Christoffer Källberg
00:20 - 00:24

Good morning everyone.

Thank you for dialing in to our Q3 earnings call.

Unknown 1
00:25 - 00:34

Please. Attention, please. The fire alarm test is now complete.

Please respond to all future fire alarms.

Christoffer Källberg
00:37 - 10:41

Apologies for that. Good morning everyone.

Thank you for dialing in to our Q3 earnings call. I will start by going through our performance during the quarter before handing over to Per for a closer look at our financials. As usual, the call is being recorded and we will publish a replay on our website shortly after the call.

What did the quarter look like? Revenue amounted to 52 million euros, up 39% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter. Gross profit increased by 28% year-on-year but decreased quarter-on-quarter. We'll cover this in more detail in the financial section. EBITDA increased 18% year-on-year but decreased quarter-on-quarter as we continue to invest in our organization. As a result, EBITDA margin dropped to 40%. Again, we will talk about this in the financial section. Free cash flow more than doubled compared to Q3 last year. In terms of games, we launched 20 new games across our studios during the quarter. The OpenRGS platform continues to expand and we onboarded 3 new studios during the quarter.

I'll expand on each of these areas in the coming slides. Starting with revenue. Revenue grew 39% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter. We see continued healthy growth in our core business.

In terms of market revenue mix, during the quarter, we can split our revenues into three main markets: Europe, Americas, and the rest of the world. European markets are large and increasingly mature. We would summarize European growth as healthy and stable. The US and the Americas, on the other hand, represents a relatively small but dynamic market and a growth driver. The rest of the world segment is made up of multiple distinct markets including regulated markets in Latin America and unregulated offshore businesses in areas such as Asia.

We haven't issued guidance for the full year, but we've adopted long-term financial targets, including a revenue growth target of more than 30%. Our strong Q3 results support our view on the short, mid, and long-term direction of the company. We've seen an increased focus from various stakeholders on understanding how companies work with compliance-related matters.

First and foremost. We are a supplier, a platform provider, and a content provider, and we supply to the iGaming industry.

We are exactly that, a supplier. We do not actively target specific jurisdictions or player demographics. As a supplier, we ensure that we have all necessary licenses and that our games are certified as required. We do this to allow each of our customers to launch our content in the jurisdictions they prioritize. As a result of that, our geographic footprint is an outcome of the aggregated strategies and relative success of our customers. As part of the IPO process, we stated that in Q1 2025, approximately 12% of our bets were considered locally licensed bets.

In other words, these bets are placed with operators who hold a local license in a locally licensed market. For the avoidance of doubt, this does not include bets generated via global licenses such as the Malta license. Hence, it is different from comparing regulated to unregulated revenues.

We consider our approach the most conservative one and thus the most relevant for public disclosure.

I would also add that in jurisdictions where we are required to obtain some form of local license, for instance the UK, we ensure that we obtain that license and that we only provide content to operators who also have the appropriate license in those jurisdictions. Under the leadership of our Chief Compliance Officer, we work actively with regulators around the world and we prioritize our good relationships with each one of them.

This work has always been and continues to be a central part of our company.

During the quarter in California, there was media coverage of a lawsuit filed by the city attorney of Los Angeles against a large sweepstakes operator and its suppliers. No hacksaw entity has been served with any complaint from a California court. Therefore, I don't think it would be appropriate to comment on a legal action when we don't have the particulars from a court. But let me take a moment to repeat our view on sweepstakes operations as outlined in the IPO prospectus.

Hacksaw does not provide games to sweepstakes customers in states where Hacksaw holds local licenses, nor does Hacksaw provide games to sweepstakes customers in any other states not backed by an independent legal opinion provided by each respective sweepstakes customer.

In terms of our business, the sweepstakes segment is a very small portion of our revenue, and there is no single customer that accounts for a material part of our consolidated revenue.

Now let's talk about our products. Our products and brands continue to expand across the globe. Our diversified portfolio of slot games continues to generate strong cash flows and demand. Our scratch games have been a huge success, especially in the Americas with our Mega Win Scratcher and other products. Our virtual sports product, meanwhile, continues to expand globally, with new markets and new customers coming online every quarter. We continue to see strong customer interest in our range of offerings.

As I mentioned in my introductory comments, strong acceleration in the OpenRGS platform leads to higher revenue, higher EBITDA, higher cash flows, and higher earnings per share, albeit at a lower margin. The onboarding of new third-party studios is positive for the business, and we look forward to our already onboarded studios releasing even more exciting new games moving forward. Next slide please.

What are the primary operating KPIs that we monitor on a day-to-day basis?

Is the number of rounds played in our games. The average bet size for these rounds will naturally vary both across markets and over time, and the outcome of those bets placed, i.e. Players winning versus losing will, by definition, vary, and in the short term, sometimes be above and sometimes below the mathematical mean.

Regarding rounds, we calculate the average daily number of rounds played. Given the varying number of days across months and quarters, the average daily rounds played in the quarter were up 50% compared to Q3 last year, which is a very positive development. Our portfolio of 268 games is well diversified, with the largest game accounting for no more than 14% of gross gaming revenue. In Q3, our top ten games accounted for 45% of gross gaming revenue, compared to 60% a year ago, and slightly better than Q2. So we're becoming more diversified every quarter.

This concludes my initial remarks on our performance, and I would like to hand it over to Per to go through our financial performance for the quarter.

Per Alnefelt
10:43 - 17:20

Thank you very much, Chris.

And hi everyone. Let's look at the numbers for the quarter.

As Chris mentioned earlier, our revenue grew 39% year on year and 15% quarter on quarter. Revenue growth in Q3 shows a robust revenue pace for the start of the second half of the year. Compared to the first half of the year. Q3 revenue amounted to 52 million, which was up 15 million versus the prior quarter. We're particularly happy about our performance in the Americas where we continue to see strong growth.

Our gross profit margin was 70.7%, which is lower than previous quarters. This is mainly driven by lower RTP plus an increased cost of services sold, which includes licensing fees and other costs. Moving on to EBITDA, our EBITDA in Q3 was 21.1 million euros. This is higher than what we achieved in Q3 of 2024, which saw EBITDA of around 18 million euros. On a sequential basis, our EBITDA margin declined from the previous quarter. The decline in EBITDA margin quarter on quarter is driven by our continued investments in our people and organization to fuel our growth.

Specifically, employee costs have increased significantly as we have expanded our teams across our studios, tech, and compliance. We expect personnel expenses to continue increasing ahead of revenue in the near future as we execute on our growth plans. This is in line with the guidance we provided at our IPO.

Now, some comments on free cash flow and capital allocation. Our free cash flow was 23.3 million, which is more than double what we generated in Q3 last year.

Our cash position at the end of Q3 stood at approximately 84 million euros, up from around 40 million euros at the end of Q3 2024. We have more than doubled our dividends this year, but still increased our cash balance by 100%. And we still have no financial debt apart from IFRS leases.

That's it for my comments on our financial performance and position.

So back to you, Chris.

Christoffer Källberg
17:22 - 18:50

Thank you, Per. We aim to generate as much shareholder value as possible, both by building a valuable business long-term through continuous reinvestment into the business and by returning excess capital to shareholders.

We have adopted a capital allocation policy by which we intend to return at least 75% of net income to shareholders, either through cash dividends or share buybacks, or through a combination of the two after each year's annual general meeting.

Summarizing the quarter. We should be very proud of what we have achieved. We delivered revenue growth of 39% year on year and 15% quarter on quarter.

Year to date, we've grown by 52%.

We've maintained a strong EBITDA margin of 40%, while investing significantly in our team to fuel future growth. Free cash flow more than doubled year on year, and we returned significant capital to shareholders while strengthening our balance sheet. Our diversified portfolio of games continues to generate strong and growing revenues, and I'm very pleased with the continued traction we see across our business.

Thank you, everyone, for your attention. We are now happy to take your questions.

Operator
18:51 - 19:26

If you wish to ask a question, please dial pound key 5 on your telephone keypad to enter the queue. If you wish to withdraw your question, please dial pound key 6 on your telephone keypad. The next question comes from Jamie Base from Kepler Cheuvreux. Please go ahead.

Jamie Base
19:28 - 22:52

Good morning Jamie. Three questions from me, please. First of all, on personnel expenses. You did address it. But, I see that it's grown over 100% year on year in Q3. As I mentioned, you touched on why, but can we talk about whether you expect personnel expenses to continue growing above revenue for the next few quarters, or if you anticipate this trend to reverse moving forward?

Then on the cost of services sold, you mentioned again the higher costs from licensing fees. Is that coming from launching again as you roll out more in the US? Is that something we should take into account in our models?

Christoffer Källberg
22:54 - 22:59

Sorry, Jamie. I lost you for a second. Could you just repeat the second question? I lost you for a second there towards the end.

Jamie Base
22:59 - 23:20

Sorry. On the cost of services sold. You touched on that being partly licensing costs. I was wondering if that's due to more US states, and if so, is that something we should factor into our models over time? So, essentially, if you continue going to more US states, should we expect the gross margin to be under pressure?

Christoffer Källberg
23:22 - 24:48

And I'll take it one question at a time since there were quite a few.

On personnel expenses, we've talked about this in recent quarters. We should not expect to see the same elevated growth rate in personnel over the next couple of years. However, we will continue to invest in the organization, and I would expect personnel expenses to grow in line with revenue approximately over the next few quarters.

On the cost of services sold, you're right that licensing is a driver. And yes, entering new regulated markets drives licensing costs.

Sweepstakes, the questions about sweepstakes and the Americas that we've talked about before remain, but it's nothing that's deviating in Q3 from what we've said before.

Jamie Base
25:12 - 25:13

That's very clear.

Thank you.

Operator
25:17 - 25:36

As a reminder, if you wish to ask a question, please dial the pound key on your telephone keypad. There are no more questions at this time, so I hand the conference back to the speakers for any written questions and closing comments.

Christoffer Källberg
25:38 - 25:50

Very good. So, thank you all for dialing in. We appreciate your support. We look forward to continuing to deliver on our strategy. Thank you all.

Per Alnefelt
25:51 - 25:51

Bye.
